title: Declarative Pods with YAML 📝
description: Master the art of writing Pod manifests using YAML.

slides.title: YAML: The Language of Kubernetes 🗣️
slides.content:
# Why YAML?

Kubernetes objects are defined in YAML (or JSON). YAML is human‑friendly, but strict about indentation (2 spaces, no tabs!).

All manifests share a common structure:
- `apiVersion` – which API group/version (e.g., v1, apps/v1)
- `kind` – type of object (Pod, Deployment, Service)
- `metadata` – name, labels, namespace
- `spec` – desired state of the object

quizData.question: What is the standard indentation in Kubernetes YAML?
quizData.explanation: Two spaces are the convention; tabs cause parsing errors.

slides.title: apiVersion and kind 📚
slides.content:
## Choose the right version

For a Pod, use `apiVersion: v1` (core API group). Other resources use different versions:
- `apps/v1` for Deployments
- `networking.k8s.io/v1` for Network Policies

Always check `kubectl api-resources` to see which version to use.

slides.title: metadata – Naming and Labeling 🏷️
slides.content:
## Essential identifiers

- `name` – unique within the namespace
- `labels` – key‑value pairs for selecting objects
- `namespace` – which virtual cluster (defaults to `default`)

Example:
```yaml
metadata:
  name: frontend-pod
  labels:
    app: frontend
    tier: web
  namespace: production
```

quizData.question: What is the primary use of labels?
quizData.explanation: Labels are key for Services, Deployments, and selectors to identify Pods.

slides.title: spec – The Container(s) 🛳️
slides.content:
## The heart of the Pod

The `spec.containers` list defines what runs. Required fields per container:
- `name` – unique within the Pod
- `image` – Docker image (e.g., `nginx:1.25`)

Optional but common:
- `command` and `args` – override entrypoint
- `ports` – declared container ports (documentation only, but useful)
- `env` – environment variables
- `resources` – CPU/memory limits and requests

slides.title: Complete Pod YAML
slides.codeSnippet:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: hello-pod
  labels:
    app: hello
spec:
  containers:
  - name: hello-container
    image: nginx:1.25
    ports:
    - containerPort: 80
    env:
    - name: ENVIRONMENT
      value: "dev"

quizData.question: Which field is mandatory in a container spec?
quizData.explanation: At minimum, a container needs a name and an image.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content: Use `kubectl explain pod.spec.containers` to see detailed documentation right in the terminal. It’s a lifesaver when writing manifests!
